title.zh: 沒人看的時候，月亮還在嗎？Google 用 105 個量子位元證明「脈絡性」就是量子優勢的來源
title.en: The Moon Isn't There Until You Look: Turning Quantum Contextuality into a Measurable Computational Advantage

summary.zh:
【總結】Google Quantum AI 團隊用超導量子處理器（72 與 105 量子位元的 Willow），把量子力學中最像哲學問題的「測量脈絡性」（measurement contextuality），變成一個可以打分數、可以當健檢指標的工程量。他們在三類「資源受限」任務上，實際量到量子策略勝過任何古典策略：魔法方陣遊戲勝率 0.9830（古典上限 8/9≈0.889）、Kochen–Specker–Bell 不等式量到 5.618（古典上限 4、量子上限 6）、71 人 GHZ 遊戲與 105×105 隱藏線性函數問題也都超車古典。這意味著「量子性」不再只是紙上宣稱，而是能在晶片上直接讀出的數字，甚至能當作量子處理器的全新基準測試。

【研究問題】愛因斯坦曾問：「沒人看的時候，月亮還在嗎？」古典實在論相信物理性質在測量前就已確定；Bell、Kochen 與 Specker 則證明，量子力學根本不容許這種「預先寫好答案表」的世界觀。但長久以來，脈絡性多半只在少數幾個量子位元上被當成哲學驗證，很少被認真當成「計算資源」；另一方面，量子優勢的證明極其困難，至今沒有任何一般計算模型的無條件證明，只有極少數在特定資源限制下可證的演算法。真正的缺口是：我們能在紙上證明分離，卻從未在真實硬體上直接把它「量」出來，更不知道多體系統裡的脈絡性長什麼樣子。

【研究方法】實驗分三層。第一層是 Mermin–Peres 魔法方陣：Alice 抽到一列、Bob 抽到一行，兩人不能溝通，得在 3×3 表格填 ±1（每列乘積 +1、每欄乘積 −1），且交集格必須一致。他們共享兩對貝爾態，依預先約定的 Pauli 測量表「量兩個、推第三個」，九種局面各跑十萬次。第二層用連續量子非破壞性（QND）測量：讓輔助量子位元連續讀取 180 個隨機排列的「脈絡」（列或欄），共 540 次測量，重複 1000 回，據此算出 χKSB。第三層把遊戲放大到多體：N 位玩家的 GHZ 宇稱遊戲（最多 71 個量子位元），以及可對應到二維方格、用常數深度電路求解的隱藏線性函數問題，矩陣規模最大 105×105。

【結果】魔法方陣平均勝率 0.9830 ± 0.0001，遠高於古典極限 8/9；另一種「三個算符全部直接量」的版本也有 0.9355。Kochen–Specker–Bell 不等式量到 χKSB = 5.618 ± 0.005，逼近理論上限 6、明顯超過古典上限 4，是歷來最佳成績。GHZ 遊戲在 71 人時勝率仍高於古典，但優勢隨人數增加而收窄；隱藏線性函數問題在 105 個量子位元時，「等效電路深度」只從理想的 4 層升到約 6 層，仍低於作者推估的古典下界。更重要的意義是：脈絡性是可量化、可用來 benchmark 的資源，它甚至揪出了隨機電路測試抓不到的細微同調錯誤。
summary.en:
**Summary:** Using superconducting Willow processors of 72 and 105 qubits, Google Quantum AI and collaborators turned measurement contextuality — arguably the most philosophical corner of quantum theory — into a hard, quantitative engineering metric. Across three bounded-resource tasks, the hardware beat every possible classical strategy: a 0.9830 win rate in the Mermin–Peres magic square game (classical ceiling 8/9), a Kochen–Specker–Bell violation of χ = 5.618 ± 0.005 (classical bound 4, algebraic quantum maximum 6), and above-classical performance in a 71-player GHZ game and a 105 × 105 hidden linear function problem. Contextuality, the authors argue, is not merely a curiosity about reality — it is a computational resource, and a surprisingly sharp diagnostic one.

**Problem:** Einstein famously asked whether the moon exists when nobody looks. Classical realism holds that every physical property carries a definite value before measurement; Bell, Kochen and Specker showed that quantum mechanics forbids assigning such pre-written answer sheets. Yet contextuality has mostly been probed on a handful of qubits as philosophy, rarely treated as a computational resource, and never at many-body scale. Meanwhile, provable quantum advantage exists only for a few algorithms under specific bounded resources — there is no unconditional proof for a general computational model — and none of those separations had ever been directly measured on real hardware. The gap was stark: advantage could be proven on paper but not pointed to on a chip.

**Approach:** Three tiers of experiment. First, the Mermin–Peres magic square: Alice receives a row and Bob a column of a 3 × 3 table they must fill with ±1 (row products +1, column products −1) while agreeing on the intersecting cell. Sharing two Bell pairs and a pre-agreed Pauli plan, each measures two observables and infers the third — nine games, 100,000 shots apiece. Second, a Kochen–Specker–Bell test in which an ancilla qubit performs 540 successive quantum non-demolition measurements across 180 randomly ordered contexts, repeated 1,000 times. Third, many-body versions: an N-player GHZ parity game up to 71 qubits, and a 2D hidden linear function problem laid out on a grid of up to 105 qubits and solvable by a constant-depth circuit.

**Results:** The magic square yielded 0.9830 ± 0.0001 against the 8/9 ≈ 0.889 classical bound; a variant that measures all three observables directly reached 0.9355. The KSB inequality registered χKSB = 5.618 ± 0.005 — close to the algebraic maximum of 6, far above the classical limit of 4, and the best such result to date. In the GHZ game the quantum edge survived to 71 players, narrowing with N but never vanishing; in the HLF problem the effective circuit depth stayed near six layers at n = 105, below the conjectured classical lower bound. Beyond the headline numbers, the authors propose many-body contextuality as a benchmarking tool: it exposed coherent errors that randomised circuit tests miss.

keyArticle.title: Quantum-classical separation in bounded-resource tasks arising from measurement contextuality
